title: Dairy-Free Blueberry Lemon Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft dairy-free lemon cupcakes with fresh blueberries folded in, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a summer morning. Fresh blueberries burst through a soft lemon crumb, and every bite has a little tang.
ingredients: 1 1/4 cups fresh blueberries, tossed in 1 tbsp flour
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat dairy-free butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mix in almond milk, lemon juice, lemon zest, and vanilla until smooth.
Fold dry ingredients into the wet mix in two batches. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in the floured blueberries with a spatula.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the tin 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat frosting butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar in two batches.
Add lemon juice and zest to frosting. Beat 2 minutes until light and pipeable.
Pipe or spread frosting on fully cooled cupcakes. Serve same day for best texture.
tips: Toss blueberries in flour before folding them in. This keeps them from sinking to the bottom.
Use room temperature eggs and dairy-free butter. Cold ingredients make the batter uneven.
If frosting looks too soft, chill it 10 minutes before piping.
Frozen blueberries work too, but do not thaw them first. Fold them in straight from the freezer.

faq.question: Can I use frozen blueberries instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Yes. Use them straight from the freezer without thawing. This stops the batter from turning purple and keeps baking time about the same.

faq.question: What dairy-free butter works best for this frosting?
faq.answer: A stick-style dairy-free butter with 80 percent fat works best. Spreadable tub versions can make the frosting too soft to pipe.

faq.question: Why did my blueberries sink to the bottom of the cupcake?
faq.answer: This happens when berries are not coated in flour first. The flour coating grips the batter and holds fruit in place while baking.

faq.question: How long do these cupcakes stay fresh?
faq.answer: They stay fresh 2 days at room temperature in a sealed container, or 4 days in the fridge due to the fresh fruit inside.

conclusion: These cupcakes are a bright, easy bake for spring or summer. I tested this batch three times in my own kitchen before the blueberries stayed put and the frosting held its swirl.
